I am old now, 79 years, and my hands are not as strong as before. This small piece of land gives us maize, and here in Mbeya the rains come well, so I must plant properly. I will put a little fertilizer — maybe half a bag of CAN that I get from the shop when I can — and I also spread manure from the few animals we keep, because that helps the soil most. I keep seeds from last year's harvest as my mother taught me; the new seeds cost too much for this small plot. My grandchildren help me with digging and weeding, and I pay one young man for a few days to help me prepare the land before the rains.
